title: Script library imports demand machine-specific absolute paths, making presets with imports unshareable
existing_state: The subroutine-library feature hard-rejects any non-rooted import: ScriptSubroutineRegistryBuilder adds the validation error 'import path must be absolute' for anything failing Path.IsPathRooted (Services/Scripting/ScriptSubroutineRegistryBuilder.cs:82-86), then requires the file to exist at that exact path (94-98). The shipped demo openly works around this — ScriptSamples/generic/library_import_demo.yaml:6-7 imports "C:\\Path\\To\\SSH_Helper\\ScriptSamples\\libraries\\string_sections.yaml" with the comment 'Update this absolute path before running the sample.' Consequence: any preset using imports: breaks the moment it moves to another machine, another user, or the portable build on a USB stick — undermining the entire point of reusable libraries, and conflicting with the app's own AppDataPaths single-storage-root convention.
recommendation: Introduce a managed libraries directory under the storage root (AppDataPaths, e.g. %LocalAppData%\SSH_Helper\libraries\) and resolve import paths against it: accept either a bare relative path ('string_sections.yaml' → libraries dir) or explicit tokens like {{app}}/... resolved at registry-build time in ScriptSubroutineRegistryBuilder before the IsPathRooted check, keeping ScriptFileAccessValidator in the loop. Add a Settings link/button to open the libraries folder, and update library_import_demo.yaml to use the portable form. Editor validation (the inline 'must be absolute' error) should be updated in the same pass so autocomplete/validation match the new rule.
user_benefit: Teams can share presets and a common library folder without hand-editing Windows paths per machine; the portable build's libraries survive drive-letter changes; the library feature becomes usable for its intended reuse purpose.

evidence.note: Path.IsPathRooted gate → 'import path must be absolute' + File.Exists on the literal path
shipped demo requires hand-editing a hardcoded C:\Path\To\... placeholder
